clearedSpotChecks.check: Do the evm2 changes from 35aa3280 to 7c9f3b6d, which v1.19.2 ships, touch the code that computes the PoolManager's arithmetic, comparisons, shifts, jumps, KECCAK256, MCOPY, CALLDATALOAD, memory, storage or transient storage?
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched twelve evm2 files at both commits from raw.githubusercontent.com myself (interpreter/instructions arithmetic.rs, bitwise.rs, i256.rs, control.rs, memory.rs, host.rs, interpreter/memory.rs, interpreter/gas.rs, interpreter/dispatch/tco.rs, evm/state/storage.rs, evm/state/journal.rs, version/gas_params.rs). Each sha256 is equal across the two commits and equal to the unit's local copy. tempo c0c9372 Cargo.lock pins evm2 rev 7c9f3b6deb23005fc84596ba1b13a6492d942014 and ruint 1.21.1, and the tempo/v1.19.2 tag's Cargo.lock is byte equal to it. web3_clientVersion on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz returned tempo/v1.19.2-c0c9372. In the unit's diff, bytecode/mod.rs changes only a test module, and ethereum/mod.rs changes the EIP-3607 sender check so that a delegated EOA is exempt only when the EIP7702 feature is on. That check runs at transaction validation and does not change any value the PoolManager computes. Tempo crates/evm/src/lib.rs, which tempo_file_diff.txt marks as changed, differs only in test assertions about precompile downcasts. So the result holds: no change reaches FullMath, TickMath, SqrtPriceMath, the CurrencyDelta slots or the lock.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1247: whether the face rounding loop on Arc (sync of the 0x3600 face, a forced native send, settle, take) can pay. Measured base fee and gas prices on the current builds, and looked for a cheaper forced send.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Code: the PoolManager's only payable functions are settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300,305), and it has no receive or fallback. _settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue when a non-native currency is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356), and paid is a checked subtraction (src/PoolManager.sol:359), so native value cannot be counted as face inflow except through a forced send. On chain at block 0x1fe0d67 I read native 2,463,481,410,521,231,626,364,284 wei and face balanceOf 2,463,481,410,521 with decimals 6, so face equals floor(native / 10^12) and the remainder is 231,626,364,284 wei. The gain of one round is 10^12 times the face increase minus the wei sent, which is at most the remainder, below 10^12 wei. eth_feeHistory over the last 1,025 blocks gave a base fee of exactly 20 gwei in every block, so even the 21,000 gas floor of one transaction costs 4.2e14 wei, about 420 times the largest possible gain. After one round the remainder is zero, and only other users' native activity refills it. The loss to others per round is under 10^12 wei of native accounting. The clearance stands.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Does the Blockdaemon build db2d22c1 or any other Arc build behave differently in the native value frame hook on the arms a native take can meet?
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran the value call probe on https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io with a state-overridden contract holding 1 USDC that makes CALL with value 1 and returns the success flag: address zero gave 0, 0x0b0b gave 1, and 0x3600 gave 0, matching the recorded 0/1/?/0 pattern. A native take in src/types/Currency.sol:40-52 therefore succeeds to an ordinary recipient and reverts only when the taker names address zero or the face contract as recipient, which is the taker's own choice. I did not query the other three endpoints, so the per-build agreement for 8e8edb7a, 602eed3b and db2d22c1 rests on the unit's log. The clearance holds for the official endpoint.
